subject: Urgent: Zenith Health — model zenith-v2 p95 spike — rollback authorization needed
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Srinivasan <maya_srinivasan@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-04-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: [ALERT] zenith-v2 p95 > 1.8s for 6m — initial investigation

Hey team,

Automated monitors just flagged a sustained p95 latency above 1.8s for model "zenith-v2" serving Zenith Health traffic (route: /generate/zenith). The spike started ~08:53 PT and it's been stable for ~20 minutes. Key facts:
- Traffic: 350 rps to the route (normal 310)
- Error rate: unchanged (~0.2%)
- CPU on pool-zenith-2: 82%
- GPU util: 68% on primary nodes (no OOMs)

I attached a quick p95 trend and one trace sample. Initial traces show longer decode time on step 9 (kv-cache miss path occasionally). No config deployments in the last 4 hours per orchestration logs.

Action suggestions:
1) Throttle non-critical low-priority routes to reduce contention (can throttle batch benches)
2) If p95 doesn't drop in 30m, request rollback to zenith-v1.9 (last known stable) and notify customer for potential brief disruption
3) Open ticket with Model Ops to check quantization artifact if we see increased token decode times

Marking internal severity: SEV-2 for SLA exposure.

--
Grace O'Connor
SRE, Redwood Inference

Attachments: zenith-v2-p95-trend-20280418.png, trace-sample-zenith-v2-20280418.txt
From: Maya Srinivasan <maya_srinivasan@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Devin Park <devin@zenithhealth.com>
Date: 2028-04-18T09:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: [ALERT] zenith-v2 p95 > 1.8s for 6m 'rollback authorization requested'

Thanks Grace — and looping in Marcus and Evelyn for decision/approvals. Devin — sorry to pull you in early; we wanted to keep you in the loop.

Quick summary for leadership: zenith-v2 (rolled 04:00 PT today) has a reproducible p95 regression affecting your production route. We're still within error budget but the p95 has breached your contractual 1.5s target and could impact observed SLAs if sustained.

As per our rollback playbook, I need formal authorization to perform a controlled rollback to zenith-v1.9 (safe window: 5 min cutover, small request flaps expected). If Marcus or Evelyn authorize, we'll schedule the change with a Canary swap: 30% traffic -> v1.9, evaluate 15m, then full cutover if stable. We'll notify you before the 30% swap.

Requested approvals:
- Marcus: rollback + short SLA carveout (allowing p95 to exceed 1.5s for up to 45 minutes during mitigation)
- Evelyn: sign-off on customer notification wording and post-mortem SLAs

If we don't get approval in 20 minutes, we'll implement throttles to the non-critical routes to buy time.

Maya
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
